text:
Winnipeg spent the summer and fall living inside a standoff. Connor Hellebuyck asked out, didn't report to camp, sat suspended, and was finally traded to New Jersey on Oct. 23 for a package built around Dawson Mercer. A month on, the Jets are 3-1-1 in their last five, and the goalie carrying them is Stuart Skinner, signed in July as insurance and now the starter. His .887 save rate looks rough, but he's +2.2 goals saved above expected, which says the shots in front of him have been hard. He made 34 saves Monday while Gabriel Vilardi scored three against Utah.

The other Jets story is history. Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk to become the franchise's all-time goal scorer last weekend, and Kyle Connor is scoring at a pace he has never sustained over a season. Our numbers like both tonight (Connor 44% to score, Scheifele 37% for two or more points), but they also flag both as due to cool. And Mercer, the man who came back for Hellebuyck, has five goals in ten games on ordinary chances. Winnipeg is down Dylan DeMelo for four to six weeks, a real hole on the right side.

Boston is the opposite puzzle. The Bruins win the chance battle (53% of five-on-five expected goals, the quality of shots each side gets), yet lost three straight earlier this month before beating Detroit and Washington. Elias Lindholm scored four on Saturday and has 11 points in his last ten games, and this one is earned: he's getting more chances, not just more luck. The season as a whole is running hot, though, with 7.8 extra goals of finishing and 10.2 from goaltending behind a +21 goal difference. Jeremy Swayman (+6.5) is a big part of that.

Watch the penalty box. Boston takes 4.8 penalties a game, and Winnipeg draws them. James Hagens skated in a noncontact jersey this week but stays out; Marat Khusnutdinov has his spot and shows up as our depth sleeper at 16% to score. The playoff race leans Boston's way, 83% to Winnipeg's 32%.
headline: The Jets life after Hellebuyck lands in Boston
